collect._urlNote: URLs are injected at runtime by .github/workflows/lighthouse.yml via scripts/ci/resolve-gate-urls.mjs, which reads the FIXED, REVIEWED set in lighthouse-gate-urls.json and verifies every path answers 200 on the warmed preview before LHCI sees it, so no stale slug can 404 the collect. Amended 25 August 2026: the event-detail pages used to be DISCOVERED from the preview sitemap, which made the audited page move with the catalogue and turned a marginal pass into a marginal fail on a 1,200 seat arena chart. The set is PINNED, not narrowed: three event pages, the heaviest first, and every public surface the gate has always covered. NO THRESHOLD IN THIS FILE WAS TOUCHED.
collect._authNote: All listed URLs verified to render without auth (HTTP 200, no redirect). Auth-gated surfaces - /dashboard/*, /admin/*, /orders/[order_id]/confirmation, /squad/[token], /verify-email-sent - are excluded from this gate because Lighthouse cannot pass session cookies/JWTs reliably in CI. Module M7 (admin) and Pre-Task 5 (checkout/orders perf) will each add their own auth-context Lighthouse gate using a recorded session.
collect._numberOfRuns_note: CLAUDE.md hard rule: 'NO single-run Lighthouse measurements (median-of-5 only)'. FIVE RUNS since 7 September 2026 (close-out C8 CORRECTED). Single-run measurements are statistically invalid for gating and produce intermittent NO_LCP / NO_FCP errors (observed on PR #40 first green-pass run: / and /culture/african both came back perf:null with errorMessage:NO_LCP, while /events scored 0.80 in the same run). Three runs were the floor that fitted the 20-minute workflow timeout. Measured on the runner on 7 September 2026, a 13 URL three-run collection took 17 minutes end to end (run 34079721873, 03:30:14Z to 03:47:35Z), so five runs need about 29 minutes and the Lighthouse job's timeout in .github/workflows/lighthouse.yml is raised to 45 minutes to hold the resolve, the warm pass and the collection. The local gate reads this value and pays the same cost on every push.

settings._lcp_timing_note: Gather-window tuning. PR #40 runs showed Lighthouse's LCP observer returning NO_LCP / notApplicable on the priority-image hero surfaces (/ and /culture/african) despite FCP, Speed Index, and final-screenshot all succeeding. The workflow header documents this as the known Vercel image optimiser cold-start issue. These settings push out gather closure so a slow-paint priority image has more time to register an LCP event before Lighthouse stops listening. Each is a Lighthouse-default multiplier, not a check downgrade: the assertion floors (perf 0.80, a11y 1.0, etc.) are unchanged.

collect._lighthouse_version_note: PINNED TO @lhci/cli 0.15.1, which bundles Lighthouse 12.6.1 (the npm registry, read 7 September 2026: @lhci/cli@0.15.1 declares dependencies.lighthouse 12.6.1 and is the latest release; 0.14.0 declared 12.1.0). The pin lives in THREE places that must agree, and tests/unit/ci/lhci-pin-agreement.test.ts fails the build if they do not: .github/workflows/lighthouse.yml (collect, assert, upload), scripts/ops/pre-push-gate.mjs LHCI_SPEC (the local gate collects with the Lighthouse this spec bundles) and scripts/admin-lighthouse.mjs. HISTORY: until 7 September 2026 the pin was 0.14.x (Lighthouse 12.1.0), whose TraceElements gatherer threw ('Dependency RootCauses failed: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading frame_sequence)'), so largest-contentful-paint-element and layout-shifts came back scoreDisplayMode=error with NO details in every report, locally and in CI: the gate reported the number and could never name the LCP element or the source of a layout shift. 12.6.1 returns both audits with real data, and scripts/ci/lighthouse-truth-table.mjs prints the element after every collection. The upgrade re-baselined all 13 gated URLs on the same local production build, per URL and per run, on both versions: docs/perf/LIGHTHOUSE-12.6.1-REBASELINE-2026-09-07.md. RE-CHECK BY 2026-11-01, alongside the exemption expiry below.

_aggregationContract._note: THE AGGREGATION CONTRACT. Read this before quoting any number from this gate. Every categories:* floor in this file, and every per-audit SEO minScore, aggregates with aggregationMethod 'median': the middle run of the collection, so the gate judges the TYPICAL run. Until 7 September 2026 (close-out C8 CORRECTED) the floors aggregated 'optimistic', which for a minScore assertion @lhci/utils resolves to Math.max(...values), THE BEST RUN (source: @lhci/utils/src/assertions.js, getValueForAggregationMethod returns Math.max for a 'min'-prefixed assertion under optimistic). That cost real hours on 2026-08-05, when CI reported 'found 0.74' from 0.72, 0.74, 0.71 and a regression was chased that did not exist, and it meant the owner was quoted best-run figures and planned against them; the C13 pull request's '0.77' and the merged head's homepage '0.76' on 7 September were both maxima over medians of 0.75. NUMERIC ASSERTIONS DIFFER in direction but not in kind: under optimistic a maxNumericValue resolves to Math.min, again the best run, which is why the event-detail budget below has pinned median on every numeric assertion since it was written; a budget that aggregates optimistically looks strict and behaves loosely. Every floor now pins median explicitly, and tests/unit/ci/lighthouse-aggregation-contract.test.ts fails the build if this declaration and the assertions below ever drift apart.

assertMatrix._note: SEO IS ASSERTED AUDIT BY AUDIT, NOT AS A CATEGORY SCORE. This entry replaced `categories:seo: [error, minScore 1]`, which used to sit in the general entry below and in the /culture/* and homepage entries. THE REASON: this gate measures a VERCEL PREVIEW, and on 15 August 2026 a real defect was fixed - previews were serving `x-robots-tag: index, follow` and publishing a 932-URL sitemap on the preview host, overriding Vercel's own noindex and offering Googlebot a second copy of the catalogue. next.config.ts now sends `noindex, nofollow` on every non-production deployment. Lighthouse's `is-crawlable` audit carries 4.04 of the SEO category's 13.04 weighted points, so a CORRECTLY noindexed preview scores 0.69 and can never reach 1. Measured on PR #118, is-crawlable was the ONLY failing SEO audit on all eleven gated URLs: the gate was failing the fix. NOT A RELAXATION: a category score of 1 is reached exactly when every weighted audit passes, so asserting each audit at minScore 1 demands precisely the same things of the page, and names the one that broke instead of reporting a fraction. aggregationMethod is pinned to `median` on every one of them (since 7 September 2026, when every category floor moved from optimistic to median under close-out C8 CORRECTED) so the replacement judges runs identically to the category floor it replaces - neither stricter nor looser. THE TWO EXCLUSIONS, both enforced elsewhere rather than dropped: `is-crawlable` is environment-dependent and is asserted by scripts/ci/assert-seo-audits.mjs against the HOST (a preview MUST be blocked, production MUST be crawlable), which means re-breaking the indexing defect now fails this gate - nothing checked that before; `structured-data` is weight 0 with scoreDisplayMode `manual`, for which LHCI's minScore getter returns undefined. That script also fails the build if Lighthouse ever reports an SEO audit outside its reviewed baseline, which is what stops a hand-written list silently covering less than the category floor did.
assertMatrix._pattern_note: Excludes /login and /signup only. They are deliberately noindex AND deliberately non-canonical (measured: both fail `canonical` as well as `is-crawlable`), and the dedicated entry below already switches their SEO category off for that reason. Every other audited URL gets the full per-audit set.
assertMatrix._expiryReason: The categories:seo floor is off because this gate measures a Vercel preview, which is noindex BY DESIGN and permanently so. That is a settled design decision, not a deferred fix, so it carries no expiry date. The per-audit assertions in this entry hold the same bar, and scripts/ci/assert-seo-audits.mjs asserts indexability against the environment and fails if the audit set drifts from its reviewed baseline. scripts/ci/lighthouse-exemption-expiry.mjs reprints this on every run so it stays visible.

assertMatrix._pattern_note: Negative lookahead excludes /login and /signup (they carry their own entry below; note this entry no longer asserts any SEO category - SEO moved to the per-audit entry at the top of this matrix on 16 August 2026) AND the homepage / (Issue #42 class per CLAUDE.md docs/perf/v2/closure-report.md flagging 'Mobile homepage and /events have known cold-cache measurement issue ... do not block on it'; see the dedicated entry below). Each excluded path has its own dedicated assertMatrix entry that re-applies whichever assertions still need to fire at error-level for that path. assertMatrix entries are independent and additive (a URL matched by multiple entries has all matching assertions evaluated), so excluding here is the only way to suppress the default error-level threshold from also firing. REMOVED 7 September 2026 (close-out C8.3): a third exclusion, (?!.*/culture/.+$), and the warn-level entry it fed. The pattern matched nothing, because the platform serves /community/* and has since the culture-to-community rename, so the waiver protected no page; and the community pages do not need it: /community/african measured 0.93 in every one of three runs on the runner (run 34079721873, 7 September 2026) and 0.93 to 0.96 on the local gate, above this entry's 0.80 floor, so the general floor applies to them at error level as it does to every other public page.

assertMatrix._note: EVENT DETAIL CRITICAL-PATH BUDGET. An overall performance score hides WHICH thing regressed: this route sat at a 0.78 median for weeks while the cause (a 187KB chunk carrying rrweb, 1,047ms of evaluation, LCP render delay 3,071ms) was invisible behind a single number. These assertions name the individual costs so a regression says what broke. They are additive to the global entry above, which still applies its own error-level floors to this URL - nothing here relaxes anything. Values carry deliberate headroom over the measured warm-preview medians (TBT 402ms, LCP 3547ms, main thread 2054ms, script 433KB) so the budget catches real regressions without flaking on runner variance. total-blocking-time and largest-contentful-paint are RAISED from warn to error at their existing numeric values, never loosened. Script byte weight is capped where it is because the split that fixed the critical path also duplicated some shared runtime and pushed script bytes UP from 370KB to 433KB: sequencing improved, byte weight did not, and this budget stops that trend continuing unnoticed.
assertMatrix._aggregation_note: Every assertion here pins aggregationMethod to median EXPLICITLY. Without it LHCI aggregates numeric assertions optimistically, taking the BEST of the three runs, which makes a budget look strict and behave loosely: the first CI run of this budget passed an error-level LCP cap of 4000ms while the uploaded report for that same run recorded 4,391ms. A budget that cannot fail is decoration. Median matches how the categories:performance floor is already judged, so the whole gate now speaks one language.
assertMatrix._lcp_value_note: LCP is capped at 4500 rather than 4000 because 4000 was not honest against measured CI behaviour (4,391ms observed on a passing run). The number is set where it actually bites on a regression without flaking on runner variance, and it is ERROR-level on this route where the global entry only warns. Tighten it when the render-delay work below 3,000ms lands.

assertMatrix._note: Login and signup are intentionally noindex/nofollow per fan-protection: auth pages should not be indexed (signed-in users get redirected away, indexing dilutes brand SEO). is-crawlable and canonical audits would fail on these pages by design, so the SEO category assertion is downgraded to warn here while perf/a11y/bp stay error-level.
assertMatrix._expiryReason: Auth pages are deliberately noindex/nofollow (signed-in users get redirected away, indexing dilutes brand SEO), so the is-crawlable and canonical audits can never pass by design. This is a settled design decision, not a deferred fix, so it carries no expiry date. scripts/ci/lighthouse-exemption-expiry.mjs reprints it on every run so it stays visible.

assertMatrix._note: Homepage / mobile cold-cache image-optimiser race - same class as /culture/* per Issue #42 and CLAUDE.md docs/perf/v2/closure-report.md ('Mobile homepage and /events have known cold-cache measurement issue to be revisited with production warm-cache data, do not block on it'). The homepage hero is a heavy priority-painted raster on mobile and trips the same Vercel image optimiser cold-start race already documented for /culture/*. Observed in this PR's run (median-of-3): perf 0.76 on /, while /culture/african produced null/NaN for perf/LCP/TBT in the same run - both routes are stuck below the 0.80 floor for the same documented reason. Performance is gated at warn-level so the score stays visible in CI without blocking deploys; accessibility, best-practices, and CLS remain at the full error-level. SEO is no longer asserted as a category here: it moved to the per-audit entry at the top of this matrix on 16 August 2026, which applies to this URL too and holds the same bar audit by audit. Restore performance to error-level when the underlying cold-cache fix lands (same fix horizon as Issue #42). /events is also flagged in CLAUDE.md as having the same issue but is left at error-level for now because the current run still measured it above 0.80 - relax it only when it actually fails.
assertMatrix._expiryReason: Homepage cold-cache image-optimiser race, same class as Issue #42. Performance is warn-level here only. scripts/ci/lighthouse-exemption-expiry.mjs FAILS the build once this date passes.
